Let the cycle vertices be ordered as \(0,1,\ldots,12\). The shortest distances from \(\ast\) are
\[
(7,7,7,11,15,13,17,21,23,19,15,15,11),
\]
and the distances between cycle vertices remain
\[
d(i,j)=4\min(|i-j|,13-|i-j|).
\]

For a zero-sum vector \(c\), write \(y_i=c_i\) for \(i=0,\ldots,12\), so \(c_\ast=-\sum_i y_i\). Then
\[
\sum_{z,w}c_zc_wd(z,w)=y^T R y,
\]
where
\[
R_{ij}=d(i,j)-d(\ast,i)-d(\ast,j).
\]
A direct exact elimination of \(R\) gives a one-dimensional kernel generated by
\[
k=(-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2),
\]
and the restriction to a complement is negative definite; for example the leading pivots on the first \(12\) coordinates are
\[
-14,\ -\frac{48}{7},\ -\frac{20}{3},\ -8,\ -8,\ -\frac{22}{5},\ -8,\ -\frac{58}{11},\ -\frac{54}{29},\ -\frac{74}{27},\ -\frac{94}{37},\ -\frac{104}{47}.
\]
Thus \(p=1\) is the endpoint unless the derivative in the null direction is nonpositive.

The normalized equality vector is therefore
\[
a_\ast=2,\qquad
(a_0,\ldots,a_{12})
=(-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2).
\]
It satisfies \(\sum_z a_z=0\) and \(\sum_{z,w}a_za_wd(z,w)=0\).

Now
\[
\tau=\frac14\sum_{z,w}a_za_wd(z,w)\log d(z,w).
\]
Grouping ordered pairs by their distance gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau={}&-7\log 7-48\log 8-22\log 11+6\log 12-26\log 13\\
&+45\log 15-48\log 16-34\log 17-80\log 20\\
&+46\log 23+168\log 24.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\tau=\log\!\left(
\frac{2^{20}3^{219}23^{46}}
{5^{35}7^7 11^{22}13^{26}17^{34}}
\right).
\]
Numerically \(\tau\approx112.9684>0\), so the null direction becomes positive immediately for \(p>1\). By the standard monotonicity of negative type in \(p\), this forces \(\wp=1\).

\[
\boxed{
(\wp,\tau)=
\left(
1,\,
\log\!\left(
\frac{2^{20}3^{219}23^{46}}
{5^{35}7^7 11^{22}13^{26}17^{34}}
\right)
\right)
}
\]
